newsitem.title: USA: Wyser-Pratte sees victory on Wallace vote.
newsitem.headline: Wyser-Pratte sees victory on Wallace vote.

text.p: Wyser-Pratte & Co expects Wallace Computer Services Inc shareholders to approve a bylaw that would limit the company's takeover defence at the business-forms maker's annual shareholder meeting Wednesday.
"We're highly confident we're going to win this one on the bylaw proposal," Eric Longmeire, senior managing director of the firm run by investor Guy Wyser-Pratte said on Tuesday.

He said most of Wallace's major institutional investors had voted for the proposal, which requires Wallace to drop its poison pill defence in 90 days if it receives an all-cash offer of a 25 percent premium over the stock's average price over the past 30 days before the offer is submitted.

Wallace would only be able to maintain its anti-takeover defence if shareholders voted to retain it. Wallace successfully withstood a hostile takeover bid launched last year by Moore Corp Ltd, saying it was not in the shareholders's best interest. Longmeire said Wyser-Pratte believes it has about a seven million vote margin on the issue.
Wallace would not comment, citing rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission. But the company has contended that the bylaw is illegal under Delaware law, where Wallace is incorporated.
Longmeire conceded that Wyser-Pratte does not appear to have enough votes to elect a slate of directors to Wallace's board but said it is the bylaw that is critical to Wyser-Pratte.
In a statement released in New York, Guy Wyser-Pratte said, that based on a preliminary tabulation by its proxy solicitor, "It looks like we won the vote on a proposed bylaw change."
Guy Wyser-Pratte emphasised that his opinion was based on preliminary tabulations that might include duplicate proxies.
He also noted that because shareholders still had the opportunity to revoke previously executed proxies and vote in person at the meeting, there could be no assurance as to the outcome of the vote.
